mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 4-week average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discount rates eroding expected future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS rises by more than 2% from the prior month, increased labor demand is expected to boost corporate profits, driving a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: Across 2005-2024, the 60-day forward return outperforms the median when PAYEMS growth is not above 2% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (units) and simultaneous decline in INDPRO (index) indicate shifting supply-demand dynamics that predict a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 1000 instances where the pattern occurs, the 5-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (supply index) below 100 for three consecutive months signals persistent production softness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In contraction phases, 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, lower long-term real rate expectations are expected to support equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 200 such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not higher than the pre-trend mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in both GDPC1 (demand spending) and RSAFS (durable goods orders) suggests resilient consumer and business demand, forecasting a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: Across 2010-2024, the 60-day return is not significantly higher than the median during such dual-proxy up moves (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% for a month predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes and devalue equities.
failure_condition: In >500 such spikes, the 5-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in GDPC1 (demand) exceeding 3% for four consecutive months indicates an over-supplied economy, which is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: In softening phases, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (p > 0.1).
